executiveSummary: Analysis of 21 surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning October 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent biological threats across Europe and the Americas. The most pressing concerns include ongoing Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas with pandemic spillover potential, a significant dengue burden region-wide, and resurging pertussis across the Western Hemisphere. Simultaneous circulation of multiple respiratory pathogens including seasonal influenza, RSV, and mpox compounds surveillance and healthcare resource demands. Yellow fever activity and chikungunya alerts further indicate a heightened arboviral threat landscape in the Americas.
bottomLine: The Americas face a critical multi-pathogen burden in 2026 with H5N1 spillover risk, explosive dengue activity, and resurging vaccine-preventable diseases demanding immediate coordinated response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained H5N1 activity
Animal-to-human spillover risk flagged across the Americas region with ongoing wildlife and livestock detections
threats.action: Enhance zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interfaces, activate pandemic preparedness protocols, and accelerate antiviral stockpiling and H5N1 vaccine readiness assessments

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 indicating high regional burden
Historical 2025 hyperendemic activity providing amplified baseline for 2026 surge
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations, activate emergency case management protocols, ensure blood product safety screening, and issue traveler advisories for endemic zones

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and Respiratory Co-circulation
threats.pathogen: Influenza A and B viruses; Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO alert on simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation issued January 2026
PAHO alert for start of Southern Hemisphere 2026 influenza season issued April 2026
ECDC weekly communicable disease threat reports across Weeks 16-20 of 2026 flagging respiratory pathogen activity in Europe
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination campaigns for Southern Hemisphere season, reinforce hospital surge capacity, and enhance syndromic surveillance for severe acute respiratory illness

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO epidemiological updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained and resurging transmission
Multi-country resurgence pattern suggesting waning immunity and potential vaccine coverage gaps
threats.action: Audit vaccination coverage rates across age cohorts, intensify Tdap booster campaigns particularly for pregnant women and healthcare workers, and strengthen laboratory confirmation capacity

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 indicating ongoing transmission in the Americas
Continued multi-country spread since prior outbreak waves
threats.action: Maintain ring vaccination strategies, scale contact tracing infrastructure, and ensure clinical recognition training for healthcare providers across the region

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active cases or spillover risk
Epizootic activity in non-human primates serving as early warning signal for human risk zones
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk populations and travelers, conduct entomological surveillance in sylvatic and peri-urban zones, and prepare emergency vaccine deployment plans

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active transmission or importation risk
Co-circulation with dengue and Zika creates diagnostic complexity and compounded healthcare burden
threats.action: Strengthen arboviral integrated surveillance, promote Aedes aegypti vector control, and ensure clinical differentiation protocols from dengue are in place at healthcare facilities

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 signaling resurgence risk in the Americas
Post-pandemic vaccination coverage gaps creating susceptible cohorts in multiple countries
threats.action: Conduct urgent supplementary immunization activities targeting under-vaccinated communities, strengthen port-of-entry surveillance, and ensure outbreak response stockpiles of MMR vaccine are pre-positioned

diseases: Communicable disease threats (multiple pathogens per ECDC weekly reports Weeks 16-20)

amrSignals: No explicit AMR-specific alerts identified in the 21 reports; however, pertussis resurgence despite existing antibiotic treatment protocols warrants monitoring of macrolide resistance in Bordetella pertussis isolates

Sustained H5N1 activity in animal reservoirs raises concern for antiviral resistance emergence under selection pressure if oseltamivir is used broadly in agricultural settings without adequate stewardship
emergingPatterns: Convergence of multiple arboviral threats (dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever) in the Americas suggests an expanding Aedes vector habitat likely driven by climate and urbanization factors

Simultaneous resurgence of multiple vaccine-preventable diseases (measles, pertussis) across the Americas indicates systemic vaccination coverage erosion potentially attributable to COVID-19 pandemic disruptions
Five consecutive weeks of ECDC communicable disease threat reports (Weeks 16-20, April-May 2026) suggest a sustained multi-pathogen alert posture in Europe not limited to single events
Dual PAHO H5N1 updates (November 2025 and March 2026) indicate persistent and potentially expanding zoonotic activity rather than a contained outbreak
Co-circulation of influenza, RSV, and mpox creates compounded healthcare system stress and diagnostic ambiguity particularly for severe respiratory presentations
